subject.title: feat(compaction): add identifier survival validation after summarization

question: Should OpenClaw accept this strict post-cap cancellation and expanded tool-payload identifier extraction once runtime proof is supplied, or should the fix be narrowed first?
rationale: The patch changes default safeguard compaction behavior and a credential-sensitive extraction boundary; automation can review code shape but cannot own that compatibility/security tradeoff for maintainers.

options.title: Require runtime proof, then accept
options.body: Ask for redacted runtime compaction proof at the current head and land this branch if maintainers accept the fail-closed strict behavior.

options.title: Split the security fix first
options.body: Land a narrower sanitizer and cap-overflow cancellation patch while deferring broader transcript-wide survival checks.

options.title: Accept source proof only
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally accept helper and unit-test evidence, but then own the live-session uncertainty around strict cancellation and redaction.

recommendation.title: Require runtime proof, then accept
recommendation.body: Ask for redacted runtime compaction proof at the current head and land this branch if maintainers accept the fail-closed strict behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The live PR requested review from steipete and recent history shows adjacent compaction/runtime work near this boundary.
